findings.text: checkpointWal reads PRAGMA busy_timeout even when waitMs is undefined, so for the two mirror.ts callers the read does nothing. Q5. Upheld as advisory: it is extra work, not a fault.

The pendingRevisions generator repeats the seq-keyed batch loop of forEachRevision (store.ts:617-631). This is round 4 F-3's remaining half. Q2. Upheld as advisory: the reviewer calls it boilerplate, not logic.

AC-49, purge over an unreadable note. The test's name says the purge replays its own folders, but the only check is that the kept file is still there. A purge that skipped its own replay would still pass. Q1. Upheld as advisory: the round-4 branch (REBUILD_MARK) is proven, and this only weakens the second half of the name.

checkpointWal. The test proves the busy timeout is put back. It does not prove the 200 ms wait is applied or that the log is truncated: dropping the set at store.ts:641, or changing TRUNCATE to PASSIVE, would still pass. Q1/Q6. Upheld as advisory.
AC-49, owed replay. The test shows the note is written before the first git call, not that it is written inside the erasure's transaction. Carried from round 4. Upheld as advisory.
AC-49, a renewal before every git call. This is proven by an exact count of clock reads, so the test is brittle to an unrelated clock read. Q5, carried. Upheld as advisory.
AC-44. Reopening the file after a failed module migration does not show that the earlier handle was closed. Carried. Upheld as advisory.
AC-49, no request waits on git. The 500 ms timing is taken with an injected mirrorChild, before any child launches. Carried. Upheld as advisory.
AC-54. The file half sits under an observed criterion, so it has no red run, as ruled in round 1. Carried. Upheld as advisory.

When the server's own export child is running at the top of the hour, the checkpoint is skipped and nothing is logged, so a purge's wal: busy debt can outlive the hour without a trace. No test covers the tick's warn line or the logged throw. Upheld as advisory: the window is narrow, it heals at the next free tick, and no client exists yet.

An unparseable note sets mirror.rebuild, but serve status shows neither mirror.replay nor mirror.rebuild, and a stale mirror.last.error can stay. Carried from round 4 F-4, not taken. Upheld as advisory: the next run heals it, and it is placed in the part 7 runbook.
publish depends on a multi-arch push whose arm64 image never runs before release. Carried. Upheld as advisory: ADR 0026 Follow-ups states it, with the undo.
WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_VERSION=0.7.0 while package.json is 0.6.0, so the image is absent until 0.7.0 is tagged. Carried. Upheld as advisory: docker compose pull shows it at once.
Rolling back across a schema bump is a manual restore that relies on part 6 clients to re-push what the copy lacks. Carried. Upheld as advisory: the procedure is stated.

Only docker ps and the runbook read the HEALTHCHECK, and nothing restarts the container on it. This line is inside the change. Upheld as advisory, not a defect: the spec states the limit itself, so no rollback or dependency is left unstated.

The feed-uid helpers stay in push.ts and the mirror imports them from there. Carried from round 4, declined with a sound reason. Upheld as advisory: this is a convention point where the base is silent, not a boundary crossed.

The checkpointWal test covers only the case with no reader. Two paths are untested: a held reader (the call should return false within the wait, with the timeout put back) and a throw inside the try (the finally should restore the timeout). Rubric Q6. Upheld as advisory: the code at store.ts:640-647 handles both correctly.

The docker job pushes the version tag and moves latest before publish runs, so a failed publish leaves an image with no release. Q4. Upheld as advisory: the undo is in ADR 0026 Follow-ups, and compose requires an explicit version.
The arm64 image is pushed without being run once, since CI runs only amd64. Q1. Upheld as advisory: ADR 0026 Follow-ups names it.
apt-get install git ca-certificates is not pinned, though the base image is pinned by digest. Q6. Upheld as advisory: ADR 0026 Follow-ups names it.

The proposed health command curl -fsS http://localhost:80/ reaches Caddy's redirect, not the server's health. Lowered to advisory: the reviewer marks it outside the change (carried debt), and the change's own check is serve health inside the container.
